title: Ploy
oneLiner: AI-native site builder that uses Jev to pick headline, layout, and copy per visitor segment in milliseconds.
description: Ploy is a marketing site product that personalizes funnel pages without running a full A/B test program for every headline tweak. Builders describe segments and variants; Jev scores which combination fits the incoming visitor context. The public launch clip on X shows roughly twenty-five millisecond decisions per visitor. Listed here as a shipped product pattern for Choice-driven personalization, not a directory stub.

title: rtrvr.ai
oneLiner: Free browser agent that records tasks; Jev speeds routing on the hot path while the LLM still plans steps.
description: rtrvr.ai is a browser automation product aimed at repeatable recorded workflows without forcing every user to bring their own API keys on day one. Community demos highlight Jev shaving latency on routing decisions inside the agent loop while larger models handle open-ended planning. Treat this listing as the product home for the rtrvr.ai domain referenced in builder clips on the showcase.

title: jev-codes
oneLiner: Standards gate for agent-written diffs: YAML rules plus parallel Jev questions before merge.
description: jev-codes is a devtools project from Kushal Agarwal that points Jev at a pull request diff and a YAML standards pack. Instead of one sprawling LLM review essay, the tool asks focused System One questions and surfaces merge-ready opinions. The showcase clip walks through wiring standards once and reusing them across repos.

title: TanStack AI decide()
oneLiner: TanStack AI ships decide() for typed Choice, Score, and boolean paths so agent loops stay structured.
description: TanStack AI is the TanStack team's AI SDK surface. The decide() helper exposes System One style typed decisions to TypeScript apps without hand-rolling HTTP clients for every question schema. Official docs live on tanstack.com; the launch clip on X shows decide() inside real agent code. This listing tracks the integration as a first-class way to call Jev-shaped primitives from TanStack apps.

title: Your Signal
oneLiner: Local feed scoring: Jev ranks posts already on screen against your rules with BYOK and no telemetry pitch.
description: Your Signal is an open experiment from Fabio Angela for ranking social feed items against personal rules on device. The builder clip emphasizes local scoring with bring-your-own-key configuration instead of shipping text to a mystery cloud for relevance labels. Listing tracks the project as described in the public showcase post while we wait for a stable product URL beyond the launch thread.

title: Magic Jev Ball
oneLiner: Playful code-review gate that bounces bad diffs; merge when Jev says yes, not when vibes say maybe.
description: Magic Jev Ball is a builder demo from Agamya that frames code review as a merge gate with visible Jev judgments. The showcase clip treats it as a teaching pattern for parallel questions on diffs before you trust an agent with write access. Primary public reference is the launch post on X until a canonical repo link is published separately.

title: Dub
oneLiner: Link management platform that uses Jev to flag malicious dub.sh URLs trained on historical abuse domains.
description: Dub (dub.co) is a modern link attribution and short-link product used by teams for branded dub.sh links and analytics. Steven Tey's public build clip describes feeding ten thousand plus previously caught malicious domains into Jev so new short links can be scored for abuse before they spread. The approach leans on Jev token efficiency so scanning stays cheap at short-link volume. This listing tracks the shipped abuse-detection pattern from the launch post, not a speculative integration.

title: Avec
oneLiner: Email client that live-prioritizes inbox threads by importance with Jev instead of reverse chronological order.
description: Avec (avec.ai) is an email product from Jonathan Unikowski's team that re-sorts incoming mail by importance as messages arrive. The public showcase clip states the experience is built with Jev and coming to Avec soon, positioning structured ranking as the antidote to endless chronological scrolling. Treat avec.ai as the product home while the app rolls out; Jev usage is described in the attributed launch video on this directory.

title: PixelML
oneLiner: Open-source pixelml-av video indexing with Grok answers and Jev relevance plus support checks on long-form video.
description: PixelML (pixelml.com) builds Composer and Sentinel agents for indexing video to text so LLMs can reason over footage. Sean Phan's benchmark clip compares pixelml-av plus Grok plus Jev against Gemini Flash on a seventy-five minute file: Jev filters retrieved evidence with local temporal context before Grok answers, then runs a support check with optional frame reinspection on low confidence. The pattern targets enterprises with large video corpora and many repeated queries.

title: Hypit
oneLiner: AI UGC creator studio where Jev picks style mixes from your product, audience, and vibe brief.
description: Hypit (hypit.ai) generates distinct AI UGC creators with natural imperfections instead of copy-paste faces. The launch clip claims one hundred unique creators in about thirteen seconds after Jev selects style combinations from a marketer's product, audience, and vibe inputs. Hypit renders the chosen mix into fresh avatars. This listing documents the Choice-driven creative routing pattern from Hypit's attributed post.

title: Egghead Smart AI Procurement
oneLiner: Japanese manufacturing procurement automation combining fast Jev browser ops with ERP systems like SAP and Oracle.
description: Egghead Inc. (egghead.co.jp) sells Smart AI procurement for manufacturers. A public builder clip highlights Jev browser automation speed for tedious ERP data entry into SAP, Oracle, and similar systems, arguing forward-deployed engineering plus Jev beats narrow SaaS alone for shop-floor workflows. The post is in Japanese and focuses on procurement use cases; this listing tracks the product domain and Jev browser routing pattern from the attributed showcase.

title: DocJev
oneLiner: OSS document classify and split library powered by Jev and natural-language category rules, with liteparse or LlamaParse backends.
description: DocJev (github.com/jerryjliu/docjev) is Jerry Liu's open-source library for document classification and splitting using TypeSafe Jev. You provide a document and natural-language category rules; Jev predicts the document category or boundaries between sub-documents. The launch post benchmarks about six times faster than gpt-5.6-luna at equivalent accuracy when using the liteparse OCR path. Optional LlamaParse integration targets complex documents via cloud.llamaindex.ai preprocessing.

title: Jev Social
oneLiner: Local Jev decision loop that drives socai CLI research in the user's Chrome and turns social evidence into cited reports.
description: Jev Social is an open-source, local-first Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn research app from socai-io. You describe a goal in plain language; the app builds a bounded set of read-only socai CLI operations discovered from live results (search, open a specific profile or post, read comments, download TikTok media, inspect page state, finish). TypeSafe Jev chooses the next typed operation each step via OpenRouter; socai runs the command in your real Chrome and returns observations. Unsupported, malformed, and low-confidence choices do not execute, and attempted ops drop out of the next choice set. There is no mock fallback, no arbitrary shell generation for Jev, and no handoff to a separate research agent: evidence compiles into cards, tables, and a cited Markdown report. Loopback UI on port 8766, Node 20+, OpenRouter key with Jev access, and the current socai CLI. Live marketing site and GIF demos on GitHub.

title: My First Million × Jev
oneLiner: Search what was said on My First Million: hybrid recall, Jev multi-question re-rank, and jump-to-caption timestamps.
description: My First Million × Jev is a channel-scoped YouTube search demo for @MyFirstMillionPod hosted on jev.aitools.fyi. Query understanding uses local lexicon plus Jev Choice intent before hybrid recall (BM25, TF-IDF, fuzzy, and caption-proximity fused with weighted RRF). One experimental_evaluate batch scores exists, relevance, topic, and hit rubric per shortlist candidate with confidence gates. The pile UI lifts matches with FLIP animation; the feature card shows Mentioned in captions chips with YouTube timestamp jumps when transcripts are enriched. Live at /demos/my-first-million/ with Cloudflare Pages Functions and a bundled channel catalog.

title: Jev FIFA rebuild
oneLiner: Shubhankar's FIFA-style soccer sim where every outfield player runs a ~150 ms Jev loop for tackle, pass, shoot, speed, and direction, plus Jev-driven commentary and soundtrack picks.
description: Browserbase builder Shubhankar Srivastava rebuilt a FIFA-style match as a love letter to real-time System One loops. Each player carries an independent Jev decision cycle on roughly a 150 millisecond cadence, choosing whether to tackle, pass, or shoot and with what speed and direction. The public clip on X also shows commentary lines and soundtrack choices routed through Jev, not a separate chat model. Peyton Casper's earlier post on the same thread highlighted a shootout-style goalie prototype from the same author; this listing tracks the full-pitch rebuild and the attributed launch video on Jev Directory. No public repo or playable URL was linked in the launch thread as of September 2026; treat the showcase embed and post as the canonical reference.

title: Jev Grand Prix
oneLiner: Local F1 sim where Jev picks racing line and pedals while code steers at 120 Hz; lap-by-lap race engineer learns corner limits between API calls.
description: Jev Grand Prix is an open Python and browser racing game from enoyola. Telemetry becomes race-engineer prose, then one batched System One request asks three questions: track position Choice, pedal Choice, and a Noul trouble meter for leaving the track. The server applies line and braking targets while the client runs physics at 120 Hz, because direct wheel steering from delayed answers caused nine off-tracks in early tests. Between laps, code remembers sector times and asks Jev once per corner whether to push, hold, or back off on a grip-percent ladder. README documents clean eight-lap improvement from about 59 seconds to 50.9 seconds with real Jev calls. Clone github.com/enoyola/jev-grand-prix, set TYPESAFE_API_KEY, and open localhost:8765.

title: Before the Fall
oneLiner: Cinematic 2D rescue game: robot S-01 saves six people in 35 seconds while Jev picks doors and actions from text descriptions, not screenshots.
description: Before the Fall is a browser-ready rescue sim from muhammadaq1. Six rooms collapse on five-second timers; the robot must clear three junctions of three doors each per victim. The engine sends Jev plain-language obstacle descriptions and capability constraints, then Jev returns a door plus an action such as push aside, lift aside, duck under, or step through. The game validates against scene rules without revealing the correct door in the prompt. A recorded run in the README rescued all six people in 28.4 seconds with 18 of 18 applied decisions and about 352 ms average API latency. Open source on GitHub with a bundled demo video; run locally with your TypeSafe key per repository instructions.

title: JEV: The Fish Game
oneLiner: Authoritative multiplayer fish arena: each AI fish batches Choice and Noul questions every few seconds while humans hunt with the mouse.
description: JEV: The Fish Game is a Node and Three.js multiplayer aquarium from muratcanberber. Up to five players plus spectators share one authoritative 30 Hz simulation with WebSocket frames at 10 Hz. Every AI fish issues one batched Jev request with three questions: action Choice (flee, hunt, eat_food, roam), target Choice, and panic Noul for sprinting. Thresholds, metabolism, spikes, and wall avoidance stay in application code; Jev supplies judgment only. README cites about 300 ms per fish decision, roughly 70 decisions per minute for five AI fish, and about ten cents per hour at TypeSafe list pricing. Host locally on port 8787 or tunnel with cloudflared; API keys never ship to browsers.

title: jev-plays
oneLiner: Modular emulator agent framework: PyBoy Pokemon Red first, with structured RAM schemas and Choice-driven tactics at System One latency.
description: jev-plays is an open Python framework from thumay9700 that wires TypeSafe Jev into retro emulators starting with Pokemon Red on PyBoy. Internal memory maps into Pydantic state objects; battle and navigation modules define Choice, Noul, and Score questions instead of parsing LLM prose. README positions the project for a YouTube series across Mario, Zelda, and Mega Man, with documented 50 to 150 ms decision targets and sub-dollar full-game cost claims versus hundred-dollar LLM playthroughs. Clone github.com/thumay9700/jev-plays, set TYPESAFE_API_KEY, and supply a legally obtained ROM per repository instructions.

title: Jev as a Judge
oneLiner: Interactive courtroom that feeds case records to TypeSafe Jev and returns rulings with confidence; Kyle benchmarked 100+ famous cases with 13% disagreement vs actual outcomes.
description: Jev as a Judge (judge.kylejeong.com) is Kyle Jeong's experiment in legal what-if tooling. You browse a gallery of well-known cases or ask the court to rule on a record; TypeSafe Jev generates an outcome from the case text alone. Kyle's launch post reports running 100 plus landmark matters and disagreeing with historical rulings about 13 percent of the time. The site labels outputs as experiments, not legal advice. This listing tracks the shipped web app and attributed metrics from the September 2026 clip on X.

title: JevRLS
oneLiner: Paste Supabase pg_policies output and compare Jev, GPT, and Gemini on the same RLS leak rubric with latency and cost side by side.
description: JevRLS (jevrls.lovable.app) is Carol Monroe's Row Level Security auditor for Supabase teams. You paste policy dumps; the app runs the same decision rule across Jev, GPT, and Gemini to see who flags risky policies, how fast, and at what cost. Site copy positions Jev as TypeSafe's System One model returning per-policy verdicts in about a second. This listing documents the public Lovable deployment and the benchmark pattern from Carol's September 2026 showcase post, not a separate open-source repo.

title: logview
oneLiner: Android log viewer with optional Jev Noul relevance filtering, keyboard TUI, recordings, and a headless CLI agents can call.
description: logview (github.com/iurysza/logview) is Iury Souza's Bun-based Android log tool. Live capture, replay, and recording share one pipeline; the terminal UI adds keyboard navigation. Enable semantic mode with TYPESAFE_API_KEY and the slash field becomes a natural-language query: Jev classifies up to 100 locally eligible retained lines per batch (default threshold 0.5), dims low scores, and keeps ingesting new lines while a query is active. Headless replay never calls Jev. README documents logview.json config, default model jev-1.13.0, and prompt version log-relevance-noul-v1 in source.

title: Jev Arcade (Netlify)
oneLiner: KP's seven-mode browser arcade on Netlify AI Gateway: color blobs, mood piano, pictionary, puppet theatre, movie guesser, things icons, plus a Jev explainer.
description: Jev Arcade at jevarcade.netlify.app is KP's (thisiskp_, Head of Community at Netlify) weekend cabinet for TypeSafe Jev via Netlify AI Gateway. Public meta describes talk-or-type play across soft color blobs, mood piano, pictionary, puppet theatre, movie guesser, and things icons, plus an info mode on how Jev and Netlify power the demos. This is distinct from the separate jev-arcade.vercel.app Krunker-style FPS listing elsewhere in the catalog. No public GitHub repo was linked in the September 2026 launch thread; treat the Netlify site and showcase clip as canonical.

title: Virlo
oneLiner: Short-form social listening with a Jev Clearance gate before eighty-signal viral video tagging on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.
description: Virlo (virlo.ai) is a content research SaaS for creators and marketers tracking viral short-form video across TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts. The catalog indexes more than twelve million clips and serves over one hundred thousand users, per public positioning from Virlo and co-founder jaffa (@dsqjaffa, @virlomain). TypeSafe Jev powers a Clearance judgment layer that decides whether a candidate video is actually on-niche before Virlo's eighty-signal panel tags hooks, formats, angles, and production cues. Clearance uses Noul-style yes/no with confidence on niche match from caption, hashtags, and transcript, plus hashtag stuffing and topic mismatch checks. Parallel Choice, Score, and Noul packs gate marketing-agent outputs such as hook type, format, angle, and worth-scripting. High-confidence rows act automatically; shaky rows escalate to stronger models or humans. Virlo (not Jev) still owns visual and production tagging; Jev controls entry into the benchmark sample. Jev runs in Calibration A/B against Virlo's existing judge; an early human-labeled head-to-head reported thirty-three of forty-four versus thirty of forty-four. Developers can reach Virlo via MCP at dev.virlo.ai and API keys virlo_tkn_* with a separate TypeSafe key for System One. Open-source Vee (github.com/Virlo-AI/vee) is a marketing agent powered by Virlo data.

title: StealAds
oneLiner: Competitor ad library teardowns: Jev labels hooks, formats, offers, CTAs, awareness stage, and landing mismatches across hundreds of live ads in seconds.
description: StealAds (stealads.ai) is Matthew Berman's (@TheMattBerman) product for breaking down competitor Meta ad libraries at scale. A public launch clip on X shows Jev analyzing seven hundred twenty-four live ads across thirty-seven brands in about forty seconds for roughly nine cents of tokens, surfacing hook, format, offer, CTA, awareness stage, and landing-page mismatch labels. The builder announced availability inside @stealads plus MCP. A Made with Jev build page documents the competitor ad teardown pattern at madewithjev.com/builds/competitor-ad-teardown. Interactive demo lives at app.stealads.ai/demo. This listing tracks the shipped marketing workflow and attributed showcase clip, not a generic ads spy directory stub.

title: Wordshift
oneLiner: Semantic typing racer: Jev judges how far apart your words are in meaning, and the car moves farther when the comparison is stronger.
description: Wordshift is Marcel Pociot's (@marcelpociot) browser game experiment described in a September 2026 X clip as the first semantic typing racer built with TypeSafe Jev. Players type comparisons such as slower than a jet, bigger than an elephant, or faster than a cheetah; Jev scores semantic distance and drives how far the car advances, so victory depends on meaning, not just WPM. No stable public play URL was linked in the launch thread; treat the showcase clip and this product profile as canonical until Marcel publishes a hosted build.

title: Box × Jev incident triage
oneLiner: Enterprise Box workflow demo: Jev classifies customer-facing impact and severity, routes files to escalate/monitor/review folders, and writes metadata.
description: Aaron Levie (@levie) published a Box plus Jev demonstration for enterprise content workflows. The clip pulls an incident report from Box, asks typed questions about whether the issue is customer-facing and how severe it is, moves the file into escalate, monitor, or review folders, and sets a metadata template instance with the result. Levie highlights near-instant decisions at very low cost and names insurance claims, contract management, loan processing, security reviews, and customer log analysis as adjacent patterns. This directory listing documents the public X workflow demo; pair it with Box's own AI and metadata docs for production deployment.

title: agent-desktop
oneLiner: Rust macOS desktop automation via OS accessibility trees; agents pair it with Jev Choice over the next safe ref action.
description: agent-desktop (github.com/lahfir/agent-desktop) is a native Rust CLI and npm-distributed binary that exposes desktop computer use through macOS accessibility trees instead of pixel guessing. Progressive skeleton snapshots cut dense app UIs down by roughly eighty to ninety-six percent token use versus flat dumps, with stable qualified refs like @snapshot:e1 for click, type, and scroll commands. The tool is not an LLM: your agent owns the observe-act loop and typically uses TypeSafe Jev to pick the next operation from a finite action table built from snapshot output, matching the pattern Muhammad Aayan (@socialwithaayan) highlighted in his September 2026 top-ten Jev repos thread. Ships fifty-eight command names, CDP interop for Chromium apps, ClawHub and skills.sh listings, and structured JSON errors. macOS thirteen plus required today; Windows and Linux adapters are planned against the same contracts.

title: Hermes Jev Skills
oneLiner: Skill pack and Hermes plugin: Jev routes models, filters memory, compacts transcripts, picks skills, and chooses GUI or browser actions without writing prose.
description: hermes-jev-skills (github.com/kerpopule/hermes-jev-skills) wires TypeSafe Jev into Hermes Agent plus Claude Code and Codex via plain SKILL.md files and a hermes-jev plugin. Documented skills include model routing (~0.4 s per turn), search result ranking, memory injection screening, turn compaction, skill selection across hundreds of installed skills, triage, mailbox sorting, and computer or browser use action Choice from operator-approved action tables. This is not tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction (Claude Code context trimming plugin), not anpicasso/hermes-jev-approvals (smart shell auxiliary), and not keeltrace/hermes-jev (async supervision nervous system). Install with python3 install.py; jev setup-key stores TypeSafe credentials in the OS secret store. Featured in Muhammad Aayan's (@socialwithaayan) ten Jev repos roundup on X.

title: 1kpapers
oneLiner: Live AI paper atlas: DeepSeek V4 Flash summaries plus Jev Choice across twenty four topics for about eight cents on one thousand eighteen papers.
description: 1kpapers (1kpapers.com) is Hassan El Mghari's (@nutlope) research atlas experiment. A September 2026 X clip describes summarizing each paper with DeepSeek V4 Flash, then sending title plus summary with twenty four topic labels to Jev Choice for about eight cents total and roughly two hundred fifty six millisecond median latency per paper. Jev topic labels may still be experimental while editorial topics show on the live site. This listing tracks the shipped atlas and attributed metrics, not a scraped index stub.

title: AI Slop Detector
oneLiner: Paste a URL: headless Chrome plus vision, thirty five parallel Jev slop tells, and a page score in about two hundred forty three milliseconds.
description: AI Slop Detector is Jon Kraayenbrink's (@kraayenJon) free scanner linked from his September 2026 launch post. The pipeline renders the page, describes visuals, runs about thirty five parallel Jev Noul questions on tells like purple gradients, emoji headers, and bento grids, scores the whole page, and uses DeepSeek for verdict copy. The public tool allows two scans per day. This profile cites the X clip and live free-tools URL, not third-party directories.

title: SuperX post scoring
oneLiner: Sixty one parallel Jev questions score an X draft in about one second; rewrite until the score peaks without rewarding reply bait.
description: Rob Hallam (@robj3d3) built a viral post classifier for SuperX using Jev on draft text only. His launch clip claims sixty one parallel questions in about one second for about $0.0004, trained on nine thousand four hundred eighty one posts from two hundred seven creators with about two-in-three accuracy picking the stronger post. Free users try superx.so/tweet-tester; the same scorer ships via SuperX API, MCP, and CLI. This listing documents the attributed workflow and metrics from the X thread.

title: 10 Jev Repos Blowing Up Right Now
oneLiner: Muhammad Aayan's ranked listicle of hot Jev GitHub projects with plain-English roles for each repo and links into this directory.
description: Muhammad Aayan (@socialwithaayan) published a text listicle on X ranking ten fast-growing Jev repositories with star counts and one-line explanations of how each project uses TypeSafe System One. The thread doubles as a reading list for browser agents, compaction, trading bots, official skills, desktop automation, computer use, code review, agent supervisors, Hermes skill packs, and Postgres extensions. Aayan also authors the X Article How to Actually Use Jev (Full Guide) at x.com/i/article/2101984233145409536. This Jev Directory guide page mirrors the ten picks with internal links to our thick listings (including agent-desktop and hermes-jev-skills, which were missing from the catalog when the thread shipped). Star counts in the original post are approximate; verify on GitHub before you quote them in a deck.

title: Hippo Memory
oneLiner: Local memory store with opt-in Jev reranking on recall so the right note surfaces first without rewriting your vault.
description: Hippo Memory (hippo-memory.com, github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory) is kitfunso's CLI-first memory layer for agents and humans. Recall stays fast and local; pass --reranker jev when you want TypeSafe Jev to score candidate memories against the query before results return. Ranking only, off by default, with README eval docs claiming recall-at-one gains on a private three hundred query set. Not a chat wrapper: Jev answers structured ranking judgments, not prose summaries.

title: NeuroLink
oneLiner: Juspay's agent SDK adds tryDecide() as a third inference type beside chat and embed, with fail-open routing when no TypeSafe key is set.
description: NeuroLink (neurolink.ink, github.com/juspay/neurolink) is Juspay's TypeScript agent framework. The decide path calls TypeSafe Jev through Vercel AI Gateway semantics so apps get calibrated Choice, Score, and boolean answers for model routing, context budgeting, relevance compaction, and tool routing without parsing chat completions. Documented to fail open when TYPESAFE_API_KEY is missing. This listing tracks the integration surface, not a hosted proxy resale.

title: jev-semgrep
oneLiner: Meaning grep: Jev scores each line against a natural-language proposition with AND, OR, and NOT composition across languages.
description: jev-semgrep (github.com/uehaj/jev-semgrep) is uehaj's CLI that filters text files by semantic match instead of regex. For each line or batch, Jev returns a Noul-style probability that the line satisfies your meaning proposition; threshold to keep or drop. Compose propositions with boolean operators; the query language and file text need not share a locale. Zenn writeup at zenn.dev/uehaj/articles/jev-semgrep-grep-by-meaning documents the workflow.

title: jev-pruner
oneLiner: Claude Code and Codex Bash hook: Jev Noul per stdout chunk asks what must stay before the model sees the flood.
description: jev-pruner (github.com/tamaratran/jev-pruner) is Tamara Tran's companion to fast-jev-compaction: it trims noisy shell output instead of transcript tool rows. After a command runs and before stdout returns to the LLM, the hook chunks output and asks Jev whether any line in each chunk still matters; chunks above threshold survive, full stdout archives locally. Distinct repo from tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction. Bring your own TypeSafe key per README.

title: jevcache
oneLiner: Local decision ledger for Jev-class calls: memoize (model, schema, state) to answers with CLI decide, recall, replay, and serve.
description: jevcache (jevcache.sh, github.com/hyperspaceai/jevcache) from hyperspaceai caches structured Jev decisions on disk instead of re-paying inference for identical state. The jev backend uses your TypeSafe API key locally; it is not a proxy reseller. Operators run decide, recall, replay, and serve from the CLI to audit what the cache hit or missed. Schemas map to whatever primitives you define: Choice, Score, or Noul.

title: foreman
oneLiner: Software factory foreman: Codex and OpenCode workers code while Jev watches factory evidence and steers completion, verification, and escalation.
description: foreman (github.com/thruwire/foreman, thruwire.ai) is Josh Rosen's Python asyncio supervisor for a software factory. Slower coding agents produce implementation evidence; Foreman runs a parallel loop that asks TypeSafe Jev about responsibilities such as implementation complete, requirements satisfied, tests sufficient, worker stuck, and needs human. Outputs drive continue, steer, stop, retry, verify, and finish. Not a replacement harness: an experiment in semantic supervision above Codex or OpenCode workers.

title: skillranker
oneLiner: Rust CLI sr ranks which agent skill fits the next step using live session context, Jev comparisons, and a real none-of-these option.
description: skillranker (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/skillranker) is Dicklesworthstone's standalone Rust CLI for skill selection. Jev from TypeSafe.ai compares candidates against the live conversation, workspace signals, and harness inventory, including abstention via none of these. Claude Code hooks, structured JSON, local feedback, and optional Quill narrowing for large libraries. Requires your own TypeSafe API key; no bundled local model.

title: jev-shell-history
oneLiner: Fish-style zsh autosuggestions: Choice over history candidates plus Noul gating before grey inline completions appear.
description: jev-shell-history (github.com/mrnugget/jev-shell-history) is mrnugget's zsh plugin that ranks recent shell history with TypeSafe Jev. On each keystroke it may send up to one hundred distinct commands with typed_so_far; Jev Choice picks the best completion ID and Noul asks whether any candidate completes the input. Prefix mode skips the model when literals match; fuzzy mode uses JEV_THRESHOLD and JEV_MIN_SCORE. History text leaves your machine for TypeSafe when a request runs.

title: neo4jev
oneLiner: Neo4j graph navigation demo: each hop is one system_one call with Choice over outgoing edges and Noul for goal reached, then beam search by log-probs.
description: neo4jev (github.com/jexp/neo4jev) is Michael Hunger's (jexp) schema-agnostic Neo4j navigator. At each node, outgoing relationships become Choice options with full probability mass; a Noul goal-reached question rides in the same system_one round trip. Top-k beam search ranks paths by sum of log probabilities. Ships Streamlit app, Jupyter notebooks, and neo4j-viz rendering against the public companies2 graph by default. Needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY for live model output.

title: jevmeter
oneLiner: Live BS and spin meter on any video: Whisper sentences, parallel Jev Noul probes per preset, rendered as a postable 16:9 edit.
description: jevmeter (github.com/ChetasLua/jevmeter) is chetaslua's open Python CLI that transcribes speech, scores every sentence with parallel Jev Noul questions from debate, earnings, podcast, or hype presets, and ffmpeg-renders a 16:9 overlay video. README badges cite about five cents for a full debate run on the battle demo post. Featured showcase clip uses remote X video (no binaries in this directory).

title: SemIf
oneLiner: Open System One style decision server: one forward pass over shared state yields Choice, Score, and Noul probabilities from models you host.
description: SemIf (github.com/TheoLeeCJ/SemIf, openjev.com) is Theo Lee CJ's independent open-source decision stack, formerly branded OpenJev on the site. It mirrors the typed question API pattern without TypeSafe's closed model: local or self-hosted inference reads option logits in one pass, returns calibrated-style scores, and stays honest that it is not affiliated with TypeSafe. Browser WebGPU demos and PyTorch paths ship in-repo; scores are research baselines you should calibrate on your hardware before production gates.

title: Simple Jev
oneLiner: Turn any open Hugging Face model into a Jev-style classifier HTTP API: shared context plus Choice, Score, and Noul from next-token logits, not generated JSON.
description: Simple Jev (github.com/featherless-ai/simple-jev) from Featherless AI exposes POST /v1/classifier semantics on models you run locally or on Featherless hardware. The server builds structured JSON from logits; the model never writes a completion blob. Public demo API at simple-jev-demo-api.featherless.ai needs no login (2k context, 2 RPS). Docs and playground live at simple-jev.featherless.ai. Self-host with the HF server in the repo when you want your own weights and keys.

title: typesafe-computer-use
oneLiner: macOS computer-use loop: OCR plus accessibility turn the screen into numbered actions; TypeSafe Jev Choice picks the next step for about $0.0002.
description: typesafe-computer-use (github.com/awlevin/typesafe-computer-use) is Aaron Levin's (@awlevin) clicker CLI for real mouse and keyboard on macOS. Deterministic capture builds a finite action list; Jev chooses operation and target in one fast call; a small writer model only runs for TYPE_TEXT, URL proposals, or final answers. Dry-run by default, --act when you trust the gate. README tables cite author-measured 155x cheaper and 14x to 40x faster model latency versus Claude Opus 5 on a bare screenshot for the same step (self-reported; rerun on your box).

title: jev-voice-browser
oneLiner: Voice-controlled headed Chromium: partial transcripts trigger one batched Jev call (~250 to 350 ms) for intent, target, safety, and scroll amount before Playwright acts.
description: jev-voice-browser (github.com/moritzkremb/jev-voice-browser) is Moritz Kremb's Node plus Playwright stack. Web Speech streams words to a local server; on debounce it snapshots up to one hundred DOM nodes and asks TypeSafe Jev a dozen typed questions in one request (intent, target element, site, command complete, addressed to browser, destructive, scroll Score, and more). Code acts, waits, asks, or ignores; Jev never generates prose, only picks candidate spans copied verbatim. Control UI on localhost:8787; API key stays server-side.

title: jev-drone
oneLiner: MuJoCo camera-only quadrotor: classical CV at 15 Hz, TypeSafe Jev advisory maneuvers at ~2.5 Hz, geometric control and safety reflex own the sticks.
description: jev-drone (github.com/RomanSlack/jev-drone, jev-drone.vercel.app) is Roman Slack's autonomous Skydio-style drone in simulation. Depth and segmentation become symbolic range sectors and obstacle height; Jev answers one batched Choice (maneuver), Score (risk), and Noul (target truly lost) call when the scene fingerprint changes. README ablation: without Jev the greedy baseline never clears station 2; with Jev engaged the author reports a full course run with zero collisions. Geometric controller at 500 Hz and 50 Hz reflex always veto unsafe climbs.

title: jev-search
oneLiner: Plain-language web search: Jev picks sources, time windows, and query terms, then Search1API fetches while Jev Score ranks snippets (no generated answers).
description: jev-search (github.com/superagents-lab/jev-search, jev.s1.dev) is an MIT TypeScript search stack on Cloudflare Workers. You type a question in normal language; Jev plans which providers, date ranges, and keyword variants to hit; Search1API returns raw hits; Jev scores relevance and returns links plus snippets only. No chatty summarization layer. Self-host with your keys or try the hosted demo.

title: Drape virtual try-on
oneLiner: Talk through a haul: Jev reads your transcript and current outfit, Choice-picks from the closet, and swaps the look on camera in about 620 ms.
description: Nailthy Tang's Drape experiment wires live speech, wardrobe metadata, and a realtime try-on feed. You talk; Jev reads the transcript plus what you are wearing, picks the next garment from a finite closet list, and the preview updates on stream. Author metrics on X cite about $0.0011 per decision and about 620 ms per swap. Featured showcase clip uses remote X video (no binaries in this directory).

title: YouTube sponsor skipper
oneLiner: Chrome extension: optional live audio and captions feed Jev a sponsor-segment gate, then auto-skips for about $0.005 per video (BYOK).
description: youtube-sponsor-detection (github.com/trungdq88/youtube-sponsor-detection) is Tony Dinh's open prototype extension. It can listen to YouTube audio, detect when a paid segment starts, and skip forward in real time. Bring your own TypeSafe key; the author cites about five tenths of a cent per video on X. MIT JavaScript repo with a madewithjev build write-up and showcase clip.

title: Internal links tool
oneLiner: Free site mapper: Jev classifies up to 500 pages and Choice-selects which URLs should link to which, exporting CSV or JSON for your LLM implementer.
description: Ian Nuttall's internal linking tool at ian.is/tools/internal-links crawls your site, uses Jev to classify pages and pick sensible link pairs, then hands back structured CSV or JSON you pass to an agent or editor. BYOK or pay one dollar to run on Ian's key. Up to five hundred pages per run. Launch clip on X is embedded in the directory showcase.

title: JevPilot
oneLiner: Three.js driving sim in Tesla FSD style: Jev picks steering and speed paths from compact candidate tables, not pixels, up to about four decisions per second.
description: JevPilot (github.com/standardagents/jevpilot, jevpilot.standardagents.ai) is Justin Schroeder's browser game where geometry and physics stay in code while Jev reads symbolic road, traffic, and destination state. Candidate maneuvers are filtered for collisions; Jev chooses among eligible paths at up to four hertz near traffic. Hosted demo meters Jev credit server-side so keys never hit the browser. Open source TypeScript with X showcase video.
